# Managed (enterprise) path manifest.
#
# A pull request that changes any [managed] or [managed_impacting] path runs
# the managed-mode CI: scripts/ci_changes.py sets its `managed` output, which
# turns on the Enterprise Required lanes in ci.yml and the Windows enterprise
# lanes in windows-native.yml. scripts/check_managed_paths.py (make check)
# fails when a tracked file whose path looks managed is in no section here, so
# new managed code cannot land outside this list.
#
# Pattern syntax (the same as scripts/ci_changes.py RULES): a pattern ending in
# "/" is a directory prefix; any other pattern is an fnmatch glob over the
# whole repo-relative path, where "*" also crosses "/".

[managed]
# Code that exists only for managed mode.

# This manifest: a change to it changes what runs, so it runs everything managed.
.github/managed-paths.txt

# Go packages.
internal/managed/
internal/enterprisebundle/
internal/enterprisehooks/
internal/enterprisepolicy/
internal/enterprisestatus/
internal/enterpriseunix/
internal/unixidentity/
internal/setuppayload/
internal/winsession/
internal/posixacl/
internal/build-repro/
internal/observability/destinations/managedaid/
cmd/defenseclaw-enterprise-setup/
cmd/defenseclaw-cmid-broker/
cmd/windows-avc-assembler/
cmd/windows-repro-manifest/
cmd/defenseclaw-scanners/

# Managed files inside shared Go packages (internal/cli, internal/gateway,
# internal/config, internal/acp and others) and binaries. The name prefixes
# are the convention: keep new managed files on them.
internal/*enterprise*
internal/*managed*
internal/*standalone*
internal/*secure_client*
internal/*secure-client*
cmd/*enterprise*
cmd/*managed*
cmd/*standalone*

# Secure Client gRPC contract.
proto/defenseclaw/secureclient/

# Packaging: MDM kits, the Windows standalone lifecycle, service units, the
# Linux and macOS enterprise packages and the AVC build kit.
packaging/mdm/
packaging/windows/
packaging/launchd/
packaging/launchd-standalone/
packaging/systemd/
packaging/selinux/
packaging/linux/
packaging/macos/
packaging/scripts/
packaging/identity/

# Enterprise build and test scripts.
scripts/*enterprise*
scripts/build-macos-bundle.sh
scripts/write-macos-bundle-readme.sh
scripts/check-assemble-parity.sh
scripts/check-repro-flags-parity.sh
scripts/generate-repro-fixture.sh
scripts/check-managed-setup-payload.go
scripts/test-managed-package-no-fleet-compiler.sh

# Fixtures and the Python tests that pin managed behavior.
testdata/enterprise-configs/
testdata/enterprise_install_lane/
cli/tests/*enterprise*
cli/tests/*managed*
cli/tests/*secure_client*
cli/tests/test_mdm_*
cli/tests/test_p0_mdm_docs.py

[managed_impacting]
# Shared code with managed branches inside, and the inputs managed packages
# are built from. Add a shared file here when you add a managed branch to it.

# Python predicates that decide managed behavior.
cli/defenseclaw/config.py
cli/defenseclaw/config_writer.py
cli/defenseclaw/envvars.py
cli/defenseclaw/upgrade_shim.py
cli/defenseclaw/windows_acl.py
cli/defenseclaw/commands/windows_uninstall_helper.py

# The enterprise Setup and packages embed the CLI and its locked dependencies.
pyproject.toml
uv.lock
.goreleaser.yaml

# Go files with the most managed branches. Any Go change already runs the
# enterprise lanes; listing these also runs the Windows enterprise smokes.
internal/gateway/sidecar.go
internal/gateway/api.go
internal/gateway/config_manager.go
internal/gateway/connector/hookexec/
internal/config/config.go
internal/config/migrate_v9.go

# The shared OpenCode adapter is embedded into the managed plugin too.
internal/opencodebridge/
internal/gateway/connector/hooks/opencode-plugin.js
scripts/generate_opencode_plugins.py

# Workflows that define or feed the managed lanes.
.github/workflows/ci.yml
.github/workflows/windows-native.yml
.github/workflows/windows-enterprise-setup.yml
.github/workflows/windows-deterministic-build.yml
.github/workflows/release.yaml

[excluded]
# Paths that look managed but do not change managed behavior. The docs tests
# that pin enterprise pages run through the classifier's name references.
docs/
docs-site/
.claude/
policies/*enterprise-data.yaml
# The manifest's own checker; its tests run through name references.
scripts/check_managed_paths.py
